extracted.intended_audience: government agencies, policymakers, researchers and the general public interested in REACH public consultations (Singapore)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how the REACH platform conducts and publishes public consultations (channels used, disclosure of findings/summaries, who receives feedback, and typical consultation durations) and how agencies handle publication and researcher access. Focused on operational publication/sharing practices for REACH-hosted consultations in Singapore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple engagement platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: REACH aims to engage Singaporeans and seek their feedback through multiple platforms such as dialogues, mobile listening points, chat groups and surveys to better understand ground issues and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage outreach across a mix of in-person and digital channels to capture diverse ground issues and concerns; use dialogues, mobile listening points, chat groups, surveys as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share collected feedback with relevant Ministries
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback collected by REACH is shared with the relevant Ministries as part of their ongoing process to review and improve policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected input should be transmitted to the policy-owning agencies to inform their review and improvement processes; REACH acts as a conduit rather than the policy decision-maker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic public release of findings of public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: REACH also periodically releases findings that may be of public interest, such as the findings from our annual feedback exercise on the Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where findings are of wider public interest, REACH may publish summaries or reports periodically (example: annual Budget feedback exercise). Use periodic publications for topics with broader public relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may use REACH Public Consultation portal to obtain feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Government agencies may also tap on the REACH Public Consultation portal to obtain feedback on specific issues as part of their policy formulation and review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual agencies decide to host consultations on the REACH portal when they need structured public input as part of policy development or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies decide consultation duration (typically four weeks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government agencies decide on the duration of their respective public consultations on REACH’s website, but it typically lasts four weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default/typical practice: run consultations for about four weeks, but allow agency discretion to set longer or shorter periods depending on issue complexity and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of findings or summaries on REACH portal at agency request
rubrics_metrics.description: The findings or summary of responses of [REACH public consultations] were published on the REACH portal, at the request of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication on the REACH portal occurs when the hosting agency requests it. Not all consultations are automatically posted; agencies choose whether to publish summaries/findings via REACH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may consolidate and publish findings on their own platforms and share with researchers as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Other agencies consolidate their findings from various feedback avenues and publish these on their own platforms and/or share them with relevant stakeholders, including researchers, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full findings may be published off-portal or shared with stakeholders (including independent researchers) at the agency's discretion and subject to 'as appropriate' considerations (e.g., aggregation, confidentiality, stakeholder relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and report consultation counts and publication rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the past five years, 126 public consultations were hosted on the REACH website. The findings or summary of responses of 49 such public consultations were published on the REACH portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain basic metrics (number of consultations hosted, number published on-portal) to demonstrate transparency and publishing practices; use these statistics to inform inquiries about disclosure rates.
